slot.brief: Mixed mole-concept + solid-state: solid with two ion types occupying different voids in a lattice with defects; derive the formula or % occupation; combine with density-edge-length to be challenging.

stem: In a crystalline solid, X ions form an FCC lattice with some X sites vacant; A and B occupy, respectively, one-quarter of the tetrahedral and octahedral voids. Given $a=5.00\ \text{Å}$, $\rho=1.56\ \text{g cm}^{-3}$, $N_{\mathrm{A}}=6.00\times10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$, and $M_A=23$, $M_B=39$, $M_X=16\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$, find the empirical formula.

verdicts.working: An FCC cell has 8 tetrahedral and 4 octahedral voids, so the stated occupancies give 2 A and 1 B per cell. The cell mass corresponds to \(\rho a^3N_A=117\) g mol⁻¹; after subtracting \(2(23)+39=85\), the remaining 32 g mol⁻¹ gives 2 X. Thus the formula is A₂BX₂.

working:
$n_A=8(1/4)=2,\ n_B=4(1/4)=1$; $M_{\text{cell}}=\rho a^3N_{\mathrm{A}}=1.56(5.00\times10^{-8})^3(6.00\times10^{23})=117\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$; $n_X=(117-2(23)-39)/16=2$; $A:B:X=2:1:2$.
